regret: Deletes every row in one statement. TRUNCATE isn't even logged like DELETE — there is no WHERE to get wrong and no undo. Remote DB state that a coding agent's git-based backup cannot touch at all.
recoverable_by: subagent (T3) with the in-place experience recipe: snapshot rows to _chats_trash, re-INSERT preserving original primary keys
baseline_blind_spot: git / cp-all / git-add see only the filesystem. The database lives in another process on another port — 0% of it is in any file backup. This is the motivating case: the sandbox is the only lane that can recover it, and only the identity-preserving recipe scores 1.0 (naive scrape-and-recreate loses the primary keys → 0.43).
note: plugin lane requires the postgres-MCP + experience wiring (see benchmarks/pg-runner.sh). The nobackup lane runs as-is and shows total loss.
